title: ZeroDL: Zero-shot Distribution Learning for Text Clustering via Large Language Models
subcategory: text-to-text clustering via aggregated zero-shot inferences (generated class descriptions)
task: Text clustering of classification datasets with an LLM
problem: When a task cannot be fully described in a prompt (no ground-truth labels), LLMs cannot perform it; few-shot prompts overfit to demonstrations.
architecture: Three stages: open-ended zero-shot inference on the whole dataset, aggregation of the outputs into meta-level class descriptions, and final prompting with the aggregated class information to assign each text to a cluster.
llm_or_encoder: mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2 (main), Qwen-2.5, Gemma-2, Llama-3.1, HyperCLOVA X SEED
baselines: Gold class labels in the prompt
key_results: ZeroDL surpasses prompting with gold class labels on several datasets and outperforms IDAS especially on datasets with more than two classes.
Generated labels reveal unseen categories such as 'Ambiguous Sentiment' and 'Mixed Sentiment' on SST-5.
strengths: Allows perspective-specific clustering (e.g. by sentiment vs topic) through text.

limitations.text: Relies on carefully designed prompts that may introduce bias.
Not state-of-the-art accuracy; computationally expensive inference over the whole dataset.
Limited range of LLMs tested; commercial models not evaluated.

notes: Evaluated on classification datasets used as clustering benchmarks; averaged over 5 runs.
